statements.subject: session
statements.description: "Session" refers to the sequence of client/server interaction from the time that a mailbox is selected (SELECT or EXAMINE command) until the time that selection ends (SELECT or EXAMINE of another mailbox, CLOSE command, UNSELECT command, or connection termination).

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: "Connection" refers to the entire sequence of client/server interaction from the initial establishment of the network connection until its termination.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Session begins from the time that a mailbox is selected (SELECT or EXAMINE command).

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Selection ends upon SELECT or EXAMINE of another mailbox, terminating the current session.
statements.trigger: SELECT or EXAMINE of another mailbox

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Selection ends upon CLOSE command, terminating the current session.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Selection ends upon UNSELECT command, terminating the current session.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Selection ends upon connection termination, terminating the current session.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Connection begins at initial establishment of the network connection.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Connection ends at termination of the network connection.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: An IMAP4rev2 connection consists of the establishment of a client/server network connection, an initial greeting from the server, and client/server interactions.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: These client/server interactions consist of a client command, server data, and a server completion result response.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: the command continuation request is still pending; the client takes the appropriate action for the response and reads another response from the server

statements.subject: server
statements.description: the server sends a command continuation request response if it is ready for the octets (if appropriate) and the remainder of the command. This response is prefixed with the token "+".
actions: server sends continuation request response prefixed with "+"

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If, instead, the server detected an error in the command, it sends a BAD completion response with a tag matching the command to reject the command and prevent the client from sending any more of the command.
actions: server sends BAD completion response with matching tag

statements.subject: client
statements.description: the client MUST send a complete command (including receiving all command continuation request responses and sending command continuations for the command) before initiating a new command.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: There are three possible server completion responses: OK (indicating success), NO (indicating failure), or BAD (indicating a protocol error such as unrecognized command or command syntax error).

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Any client command with a protocol syntax error, including (but not limited to) missing or extraneous spaces or arguments, SHOULD be rejected and the client given a BAD server completion response.
statements.trigger: protocol syntax error in client command
actions: send BAD completion response to client

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The protocol receiver of an IMAP4rev2 client reads a response line from the server. It then takes action on the response based upon the first token of the response, which can be a tag, a "*", or a "+".
actions: dispatch on token type: tag | untagged (*) | continuation (+)

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The server completion result response is tagged with the same tag as the client command that began the operation. Thus, if more than one command is in progress, the tag in a server completion response identifies the command to which the response applies.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: $Junk and $NotJunk are mutually exclusive. If more than one of these is set for a message, the client MUST treat it as if none are set, and it SHOULD unset both of them on the IMAP server.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: \Deleted: Message is 'deleted' for removal by later EXPUNGE.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: A flag can be permanent or session-only on a per-flag basis. Permanent flags are those that the client can add or remove from the message flags permanently; concurrent and subsequent sessions will see any change in permanent flags. Changes to session flags are valid only in that session.
statements.guard_semantics: flag.scope = permanent => visible_across_sessions | flag.scope = session-only => visible_in_current_session_only

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: an IMAP4rev2 connection is in one of four states

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The initial state is identified in the server greeting.
actions: server sends greeting identifying initial state

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: It is a protocol error for the client to attempt a command while the connection is in an inappropriate state, and the server will respond with a BAD or NO (depending upon server implementation) command completion result.
statements.trigger: client attempts command in inappropriate state
actions: server responds with BAD or NO command completion result

statements.subject: session
statements.description: In the not authenticated state, the client MUST supply authentication credentials before most commands will be permitted. This state is entered when a connection starts unless the connection has been pre-authenticated.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: This state is entered when a connection starts unless the connection has been pre-authenticated.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: This state is entered when a connection starts unless the connection has been pre-authenticated.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: In the not authenticated state, the client MUST supply authentication credentials before most commands will be permitted.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: In the authenticated state, the client is authenticated and MUST select a mailbox to access before commands that affect messages will be permitted.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: This state is entered when a pre-authenticated connection starts.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: This state is entered when acceptable authentication credentials have been provided.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: This state is entered after an error in selecting a mailbox.
actions: remain in or re-enter Authenticated state

statements.subject: session
statements.description: This state is entered after a successful CLOSE command.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: This state is entered after a successful UNSELECT command.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The client is authenticated and MUST select a mailbox to access before commands that affect messages will be permitted.
statements.guard_semantics: session.state = Authenticated => commands_affecting_messages require session.mailbox_selected = true

statements.subject: session
statements.description: In a selected state, a mailbox has been selected to access. This state is entered when a mailbox has been successfully selected.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: This state is entered when a mailbox has been successfully selected.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: In the logout state, the connection is being terminated. This state can be entered as a result of a client request (via the LOGOUT command) or by unilateral action on the part of either the client or the server.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Not Authenticated state shown in the IMAP state diagram.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Authenticated state shown in the IMAP state diagram.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Selected state shown in the IMAP state diagram.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: connection established — the initial condition shown at the top of the IMAP state diagram.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: server greeting — the intermediate step between connection establishment and the first stable protocol state, shown in the IMAP state diagram.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: both sides close the connection — the terminal state shown at the bottom of the IMAP state diagram.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: connection established leads to server greeting (top of state diagram).

statements.subject: session
statements.description: (1) connection without pre-authentication (OK greeting) — server greeting transitions to Not Authenticated.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: (2) pre-authenticated connection (PREAUTH greeting) — server greeting transitions to Authenticated.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: (3) rejected connection (BYE greeting) — server greeting transitions to Logout.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: (4) successful LOGIN or AUTHENTICATE command — Not Authenticated transitions to Authenticated.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: (7) LOGOUT command, server shutdown, or connection closed — Not Authenticated transitions to Logout.
statements.trigger: LOGOUT command | server shutdown | connection closed

statements.subject: session
statements.description: (5) successful SELECT or EXAMINE command — Authenticated transitions to Selected.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: (7) LOGOUT command, server shutdown, or connection closed — Authenticated transitions to Logout.
statements.trigger: LOGOUT command | server shutdown | connection closed

statements.subject: session
statements.description: (6) CLOSE or UNSELECT command, unsolicited CLOSED response code, or failed SELECT or EXAMINE command — Selected transitions back to Authenticated.
statements.trigger: CLOSE command | UNSELECT command | unsolicited CLOSED response code | failed SELECT or EXAMINE command

statements.subject: session
statements.description: (7) LOGOUT command, server shutdown, or connection closed — Selected transitions to Logout.
statements.trigger: LOGOUT command | server shutdown | connection closed

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: From Logout state, both sides close the connection (terminal transition shown at bottom of state diagram).

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the client requests the logout state, the server MUST send an untagged BYE response and a tagged OK response to the LOGOUT command before the server closes the connection; and the client MUST read the tagged OK response to the LOGOUT command before the client closes the connection.
actions: server sends tagged OK response to LOGOUT command

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A server SHOULD NOT unilaterally close the connection without first sending an untagged BYE response that contains the reason for doing so.
actions: server sends untagged BYE response with reason

statements.subject: client
statements.description: A client SHOULD NOT unilaterally close the connection; instead, it SHOULD issue a LOGOUT command. If the server detects that the client has unilaterally closed the connection, the server MAY omit the untagged BYE response and simply close its connection.
statements.trigger: server detects client unilateral connection close
actions: server may omit untagged BYE response

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A server MUST send mailbox size updates automatically if a mailbox size change is observed during the processing of a command.
actions: send EXISTS response with updated mailbox size

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A server SHOULD send message flag updates automatically, without requiring the client to request such updates explicitly.
actions: send unsolicited message flag update response

statements.subject: server
statements.description: It is NOT permitted to send an EXISTS response that would reduce the number of messages in the mailbox; only the EXPUNGE response can do this.
statements.guard_semantics: Only EXPUNGE response may reduce mailbox message count; EXISTS response must not reduce message count

statements.subject: client
statements.description: A client implementation MUST remember mailbox size updates. It MUST NOT assume that any command after the initial mailbox selection will return the size of the mailbox.
statements.guard_semantics: client.mailbox_size must be maintained and updated from unsolicited server responses

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Server implementations are permitted to send an untagged response (except for EXPUNGE) while there is no command in progress.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Server implementations are permitted to send an untagged response (except for EXPUNGE) while there is no command in progress.
statements.guard_semantics: EXPUNGE is excluded when command_in_progress = false

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: If a server has an inactivity autologout timer that applies to sessions after authentication, the duration of that timer MUST be at least 30 minutes.

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: The receipt of any command from the client during that interval resets the autologout timer.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Inactivity autologout timer applies to sessions after authentication; timer expiry causes autologout.

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: This specification doesn't have any restrictions on an autologout timer used before successful client authentication. Servers are allowed to use a shortened pre-authentication timer to protect themselves from Denial-of-Service attacks.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Servers are allowed to use a shortened pre-authentication timer to protect themselves from Denial-of-Service attacks.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client MAY send another command without waiting for the completion result response of a command, subject to ambiguity rules and flow control constraints on the underlying data stream.
statements.trigger: client sends additional command without waiting for completion result

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A server MAY begin processing another command before processing the current command to completion, subject to ambiguity rules.
statements.trigger: server begins processing next command before current command completes

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Any command continuation request responses and command continuations MUST be negotiated before any subsequent command is initiated.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the server detects a possible ambiguity, it MUST execute commands to completion in the order given by the client.
statements.trigger: ambiguity detected in pipelined command sequence
actions: execute commands to completion in order given by client

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the client sends any command other than FETCH, STORE, or SEARCH, it MUST wait for the completion result response before sending a command with message sequence numbers.
statements.trigger: client sends command other than FETCH, STORE, or SEARCH
statements.pre_cond: command_type != FETCH & command_type != STORE & command_type != SEARCH
actions: wait for completion result response before sending command with message sequence numbers

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the client sends a UID command, it MUST wait for a completion result response before sending a command that uses message sequence numbers.
actions: wait for completion result response before sending command with message sequence numbers

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Servers are prohibited from sending EXPUNGE responses while any of FETCH, STORE, or SEARCH commands are in progress.
statements.guard_semantics: EXPUNGE response prohibited when command_in_progress = FETCH | command_in_progress = STORE | command_in_progress = SEARCH

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Commands are organized by the state in which the command is permitted. Commands valid in authenticated and selected states are listed in the authenticated state commands (minimum permitted state).

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Commands are organized by the state in which the command is permitted. Commands valid in authenticated and selected states are listed in the authenticated state commands (minimum permitted state).

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The state of a connection is only changed by successful commands that are documented as changing state.
actions: update connection state to documented target state

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: A rejected command (BAD response) never changes the state of the connection or of the selected mailbox.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: A failed command (NO response) generally does not change the state of the connection or of the selected mailbox, with the exception of the SELECT and EXAMINE commands.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: A failed command (NO response) generally does not change the state of the connection or of the selected mailbox, with the exception of the SELECT and EXAMINE commands.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The CAPABILITY command is valid in any state.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The NOOP command is valid in any state.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The LOGOUT command is valid in any state.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Result: OK - capability completed. The server MUST send a single untagged CAPABILITY response with "IMAP4rev2" as one of the listed capabilities before the (tagged) OK response.
actions: send untagged CAPABILITY response with IMAP4rev2 listed

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Result: BAD - arguments invalid

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Client and server implementations MUST implement the STARTTLS (Section 6.2.1) capability on cleartext ports.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Client and server implementations MUST implement the LOGINDISABLED capability on cleartext ports.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Client and server implementations MUST also implement AUTH=PLAIN (described in [PLAIN]) capability on both cleartext and Implicit TLS ports.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The NOOP command always succeeds. It does nothing.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The NOOP command can also be used to reset any inactivity autologout timer on the server.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Since any command can return a status update as untagged data, the NOOP command can be used as a periodic poll for new messages or message status updates during a period of inactivity.
actions: send untagged status updates (e.g. EXPUNGE, EXISTS, FETCH)

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Server and client then close the connection after LOGOUT OK response, representing the terminal end of a session.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The LOGOUT command informs the server that the client is done with the connection. The server MUST send a BYE untagged response before the (tagged) OK response, and then close the network connection.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MUST send a BYE untagged response before the (tagged) OK response.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: In the not authenticated state, the AUTHENTICATE or LOGIN command establishes authentication and enters the authenticated state.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The AUTHENTICATE or LOGIN command establishes authentication and enters the authenticated state.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The AUTHENTICATE command establishes authentication and enters the authenticated state.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The LOGIN command uses a conventional user name and plaintext password pair and enters the authenticated state.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The STARTTLS command is an alternative form of establishing session privacy protection and integrity checking but does not by itself establish authentication or enter the authenticated state.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Once authenticated (including as anonymous), it is not possible to re-enter not authenticated state.
statements.guard_semantics: Once session.authentication_established = true, session.state = not_authenticated is forbidden

statements.subject: session
statements.description: In addition to the universal commands (CAPABILITY, NOOP, and LOGOUT), the following commands are valid in the not authenticated state: STARTTLS, AUTHENTICATE, and LOGIN.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: After successful TLS negotiation, the server remains in the non-authenticated state, even if client credentials are supplied during the TLS negotiation.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: A TLS negotiation begins immediately after the CRLF at the end of the tagged OK response from the server. After successful TLS negotiation, the server remains in the non-authenticated state.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MUST always respond with a tagged BAD response when the STARTTLS command is received on an Implicit TLS port.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: BAD - STARTTLS received after a successful TLS negotiation or arguments invalid.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Once a client issues a STARTTLS command, it MUST NOT issue further commands until a server response is seen and the TLS negotiation is complete.
statements.guard_semantics: While pending_starttls = true, client MUST NOT issue further commands

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Once TLS has been started, the client MUST discard cached information about server capabilities and SHOULD reissue the CAPABILITY command.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MAY advertise different capabilities and, in particular, SHOULD NOT advertise the STARTTLS capability, after a successful STARTTLS command.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: OK - authenticate completed, now in authenticated state

statements.subject: session
statements.description: OK - authenticate completed, now in authenticated state
actions: security layer takes effect immediately if negotiated

statements.subject: session
statements.description: NO - authenticate failure: unsupported authentication mechanism, credentials rejected. If an AUTHENTICATE command fails with a NO response, the client MAY try another authentication mechanism by issuing another AUTHENTICATE command.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: BAD - command unknown or arguments invalid, authentication exchange canceled

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If the client wishes to cancel an authentication exchange, it issues a line consisting of a single "*". If the server receives such a response, ... it MUST reject the AUTHENTICATE command by sending a tagged BAD response.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If the server receives an invalid base64 string (e.g., characters outside the base64 alphabet or non-terminal "="), it MUST reject the AUTHENTICATE command by sending a tagged BAD response.
statements.trigger: server receives invalid base64 in authentication exchange

statements.subject: session
statements.description: OK - login completed, now in authenticated state

statements.subject: session
statements.description: OK - login completed, now in authenticated state
actions: optionally include CAPABILITY response code in tagged OK

statements.subject: session
statements.description: NO - login failure: user name or password rejected

statements.subject: session
statements.description: BAD - command unknown or arguments invalid

statements.subject: client
statements.description: A client implementation MUST NOT send a LOGIN command if the LOGINDISABLED capability is advertised.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Clients MUST NOT use LOGIN on unsecure networks. Unless the client is accessing IMAP service on an Implicit TLS port, the STARTTLS command has been negotiated, or some other mechanism that protects the session from password snooping has been provided.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: In the authenticated state, commands that manipulate mailboxes as atomic entities are permitted.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: SELECT and EXAMINE will select a mailbox for access and enter the selected state.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: SELECT will select a mailbox for access and enter the selected state.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: EXAMINE will select a mailbox for access and enter the selected state.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: In addition to the universal commands (CAPABILITY, NOOP, and LOGOUT), the following commands are valid in the authenticated state: ENABLE, SELECT, EXAMINE, NAMESPACE, CREATE, DELETE, RENAME, SUBSCRIBE, UNSUBSCRIBE, LIST, STATUS, APPEND, and IDLE.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The ENABLE command is only valid in the authenticated state, before any mailbox is selected.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The ENABLE command is only valid in the authenticated state, before any mailbox is selected. If the ENABLE command is successful, the server MUST send an untagged ENABLED response.
actions: server enables each supported and permitted extension for duration of connection
server sends untagged ENABLED response listing all newly enabled extensions

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Clients MUST NOT issue ENABLE once they SELECT/EXAMINE a mailbox.
statements.guard_semantics: ENABLE is only permitted when no mailbox has been selected (SELECT/EXAMINE not yet issued in current state)

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Once enabled using ENABLE, each extension remains active until the IMAP connection is closed. Once an extension is enabled, there is no way to disable it.
actions: all enabled extensions deactivated on connection close

statements.subject: session
statements.description: There are no limitations on pipelining ENABLE. For example, it is possible to send ENABLE and then immediately SELECT, or a LOGIN immediately followed by ENABLE.
actions: client sends SELECT command without waiting for ENABLE response

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The ENABLE command can be issued multiple times in a session. It is additive.
statements.pre_cond: protocol.state = Authenticated & session.mailbox_selected = false & session.enable_issued_previously = true
actions: server enables additional capabilities from new ENABLE command
server sends untagged ENABLED response listing only extensions enabled by this command

statements.subject: session
statements.description: OK - select completed, now in selected state

statements.subject: session
statements.description: NO - select failure, now in authenticated state: no such mailbox, can't access mailbox

statements.subject: session
statements.description: OK - select completed, now in selected state

statements.subject: session
statements.description: NO - select failure, now in authenticated state: no such mailbox, can't access mailbox

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The SELECT command automatically deselects any currently selected mailbox before attempting the new selection. When deselecting a selected mailbox, the server MUST return an untagged OK response with the '[CLOSED]' response code. Result: OK - select completed, now in selected state.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The SELECT command automatically deselects any currently selected mailbox before attempting the new selection. Consequently, if a mailbox is selected and a SELECT command that fails is attempted, no mailbox is selected. When deselecting a selected mailbox, the server MUST return an untagged OK response with the '[CLOSED]' response code.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Only one mailbox can be selected at a time in a connection; simultaneous access to multiple mailboxes requires multiple connections.
statements.guard_semantics: At most one mailbox may be in the selected state per connection at any time

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Result: OK - examine completed, now in selected state

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Result: NO - examine failure, now in authenticated state: no such mailbox, can't access mailbox

statements.subject: session
statements.description: examine completed, now in selected state; selected mailbox is identified as read-only

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The text of the tagged OK response to the EXAMINE command MUST begin with the '[READ-ONLY]' response code.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Result: OK - create completed

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Result: NO - create failure: can't create mailbox with that name. Any error in creation will return a tagged NO response.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Result: BAD - command unknown or arguments invalid

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If a client attempts to create a UTF-8 mailbox name that is not a valid Net-Unicode name, the server MUST reject the creation or convert the name to Net-Unicode prior to creating the mailbox.
statements.trigger: CREATE with invalid Net-Unicode mailbox name
actions: convert name to Net-Unicode and proceed

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the server decides to convert (normalize) the name, it SHOULD return an untagged LIST with an OLDNAME extended data item.
statements.trigger: server normalizes mailbox name during CREATE
actions: send untagged LIST with OLDNAME extended data item

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Result: OK - create completed / NO - create failure / BAD - command unknown or arguments invalid

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Result: OK - delete completed. A tagged OK response is returned only if the mailbox has been deleted.
statements.pre_cond: protocol.state = Authenticated & mailbox.exists = true & mailbox.name != INBOX & mailbox.hasNoselect_with_inferiors = false

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Result: NO - delete failure: can't delete mailbox with that name. It is an error to attempt to delete INBOX or a mailbox name that does not exist.
statements.pre_cond: protocol.state = Authenticated & (mailbox.exists = false | mailbox.name = INBOX | mailbox.hasNoselect_with_inferiors = true)

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Result: BAD - command unknown or arguments invalid.
statements.trigger: DELETE command received with invalid arguments

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the server implementation does not permit deleting the name while inferior hierarchical names exist, then it SHOULD disallow the DELETE command by returning a tagged NO response. The NO response SHOULD include the HASCHILDREN response code.
statements.trigger: DELETE command received for mailbox with inferior hierarchical names
statements.pre_cond: protocol.state = Authenticated & mailbox.has_inferior_names = true & mailbox.Noselect = false
actions: send tagged NO response with HASCHILDREN response code

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Alternatively, the server MAY allow the DELETE command, but it sets the \Noselect mailbox name attribute for that name.
statements.trigger: DELETE command received for mailbox with inferior hierarchical names
statements.pre_cond: protocol.state = Authenticated & mailbox.has_inferior_names = true & mailbox.Noselect = false

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the server decides to convert (normalize) the mailbox name, it SHOULD return an untagged LIST with the "\NonExistent" attribute and OLDNAME extended data item.
statements.trigger: DELETE command received with mailbox name requiring normalization
actions: send untagged LIST response with \NonExistent attribute and OLDNAME data item

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Mailboxes deleted in one IMAP session MAY be announced to other IMAP sessions using an unsolicited LIST response, containing the "\NonExistent" attribute.
actions: send unsolicited LIST response with \NonExistent attribute to other sessions

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The SUBSCRIBE command returns a tagged OK response if the subscription is successful or if the mailbox is already subscribed.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: SUBSCRIBE Result: NO - subscribe failure: can't subscribe to that name.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: SUBSCRIBE Result: BAD - command unknown or arguments invalid.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Result: OK - list completed

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Result: NO - list failure: can't list that reference or mailbox name

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Result: BAD - command unknown or arguments invalid
statements.trigger: LIST command unknown or arguments invalid

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A server MUST respond to options it does not recognize with a BAD response.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Any syntactically valid pattern that is not accepted by a server for any reason MUST be silently ignored, i.e., it results in no LIST responses, and the LIST command still returns a tagged OK response.
statements.trigger: LIST command with unacceptable but syntactically valid pattern

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The RECURSIVEMATCH option MUST NOT occur as the only selection option (or only with REMOTE), as it only makes sense when other selection options are also used.
statements.guard_semantics: RECURSIVEMATCH must be accompanied by at least one selection option other than REMOTE

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MUST return a BAD tagged response when RECURSIVEMATCH is the only selection option or is used only with REMOTE.
statements.trigger: LIST command received with RECURSIVEMATCH as sole selection option or combined only with REMOTE

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The CHILDINFO extended data item MUST NOT be returned unless the client has specified the RECURSIVEMATCH selection option.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Servers SHOULD only return a non-matching mailbox name along with CHILDINFO if at least one matching child is not also being returned. That is, servers SHOULD suppress redundant CHILDINFO responses.
statements.pre_cond: client.selection_option = RECURSIVEMATCH & mailbox.matches_selection = false & mailbox.has_matching_child = true
actions: suppress CHILDINFO when matching child is already returned

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Mailbox does not exist, does not meet selection criteria, has no child meeting selection criteria: no LIST response returned.
statements.pre_cond: mailbox.exists = false & mailbox.meets_selection = false & mailbox.has_matching_child = false

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Mailbox exists, does not meet selection criteria, has no child meeting selection criteria: no LIST response returned.
statements.pre_cond: mailbox.exists = true & mailbox.meets_selection = false & mailbox.has_matching_child = false

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Mailbox does not exist, meets selection criteria, has no child meeting criteria: return (\NonExistent <attr>).
statements.pre_cond: mailbox.exists = false & mailbox.meets_selection = true & mailbox.has_matching_child = false
actions: return LIST entry with \NonExistent and selection attribute

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Mailbox exists, meets selection criteria, has no child meeting criteria: return (<attr>).
statements.pre_cond: mailbox.exists = true & mailbox.meets_selection = true & mailbox.has_matching_child = false
actions: return LIST entry with selection attribute

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Mailbox does not exist, does not meet selection criteria, has a child meeting criteria: return (\NonExistent) + CHILDINFO.
statements.pre_cond: mailbox.exists = false & mailbox.meets_selection = false & mailbox.has_matching_child = true & client.selection_option = RECURSIVEMATCH
actions: return LIST entry with \NonExistent and CHILDINFO extended data item

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Mailbox exists, does not meet selection criteria, has a child meeting criteria: return () + CHILDINFO.
statements.pre_cond: mailbox.exists = true & mailbox.meets_selection = false & mailbox.has_matching_child = true & client.selection_option = RECURSIVEMATCH
actions: return LIST entry with empty attributes and CHILDINFO extended data item

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Mailbox does not exist, meets selection criteria, has a child meeting criteria: return (\NonExistent <attr>) + CHILDINFO.
statements.pre_cond: mailbox.exists = false & mailbox.meets_selection = true & mailbox.has_matching_child = true & client.selection_option = RECURSIVEMATCH
statements.post_cond: response.attributes = NonExistent | response.attributes = selection_attr & response.includes_CHILDINFO = true
actions: return LIST entry with \NonExistent, selection attribute, and CHILDINFO extended data item

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Mailbox exists, meets selection criteria, has a child meeting criteria: return (<attr>) + CHILDINFO.
statements.pre_cond: mailbox.exists = true & mailbox.meets_selection = true & mailbox.has_matching_child = true & client.selection_option = RECURSIVEMATCH
actions: return LIST entry with selection attribute and CHILDINFO extended data item

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The STATUS command requests the status of the indicated mailbox. It does not change the currently selected mailbox, nor does it affect the state of any messages in the queried mailbox. Result: OK - status completed.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The STATUS command does not change the currently selected mailbox; servers MUST be able to execute the STATUS command on the selected mailbox.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Result: NO - status failure: no status for that name. The STATUS command fails without changing state.
statements.trigger: STATUS command with unresolvable mailbox name

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Result: BAD - command unknown or arguments invalid. The STATUS command fails without changing state.
statements.trigger: STATUS command with unknown command or invalid arguments

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The STATUS command SHOULD NOT be used on the currently selected mailbox, but servers MUST be able to execute the STATUS command on the selected mailbox.
statements.guard_semantics: STATUS is permitted in both Authenticated and Selected states; SHOULD NOT target currently selected mailbox but server MUST support it

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Result: OK - append completed. On successful completion of an APPEND, the server returns an APPENDUID response code.
actions: send tagged OK with APPENDUID response code

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Result: NO - append error: can't append to that mailbox, error in flags or date/time or message text.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Result: BAD - command unknown or arguments invalid.
statements.trigger: APPEND command with unknown or invalid arguments

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the destination mailbox does not exist, a server MUST return an error and MUST NOT automatically create the mailbox. Unless it is certain that the destination mailbox cannot be created, the server MUST send the response code [TRYCREATE] as the prefix of the text of the tagged NO response.
statements.trigger: APPEND command (destination mailbox does not exist)
actions: send tagged NO with [TRYCREATE] response code

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the append is unsuccessful for any reason, the mailbox MUST be restored to its state before the APPEND attempt (other than possibly keeping the changed mailbox's UIDNEXT value); no partial appending is permitted.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the mailbox is currently selected, normal new message actions SHOULD occur. Specifically, the server SHOULD notify the client immediately via an untagged EXISTS response. If the server does not do so, the client MAY issue a NOOP command after one or more APPEND commands.
statements.trigger: APPEND command success (mailbox is currently selected)

statements.subject: server
statements.description: In the case of a mailbox that has permissions set so that the client can APPEND to the mailbox, but not SELECT or EXAMINE it, the server MUST NOT send an APPENDUID response code as it would disclose information about the mailbox.
statements.guard_semantics: session.can_append = true & session.can_select = false & session.can_examine = false

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the server decides to convert (normalize) the mailbox name, it SHOULD return an untagged LIST with an OLDNAME extended data item, with the OLDNAME value being the supplied mailbox name and the name parameter being the normalized mailbox name.
statements.trigger: APPEND command with mailbox name normalization
actions: send untagged LIST with OLDNAME extended data item

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The IDLE command remains active until the client responds to the continuation, and as long as an IDLE command is active, the server is now free to send untagged EXISTS, EXPUNGE, FETCH, and other responses at any time.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The IDLE command is sent from the client to the server when the client is ready to accept unsolicited update messages. The server requests a response to the IDLE command using the continuation ('+') response.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The IDLE command is terminated by the receipt of a 'DONE' continuation from the client; such response satisfies the server's continuation request. At that point, the server MAY send any remaining queued untagged responses and then MUST immediately send the tagged response to the IDLE command and prepare to process other commands.
actions: server sends remaining queued untagged responses
server sends tagged OK response to IDLE command
server prepares to process other commands

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MAY consider a client inactive if it has an IDLE command running, and if such a server has an inactivity timeout, it MAY log the client off implicitly at the end of its timeout period.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client MUST NOT send a command while the server is waiting for the DONE, since the server will not be able to distinguish a command from a continuation.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: In the selected state, commands that manipulate messages in a mailbox are permitted.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: In addition to the universal commands (CAPABILITY, NOOP, and LOGOUT), and the authenticated state commands (SELECT, EXAMINE, NAMESPACE, CREATE, DELETE, RENAME, SUBSCRIBE, UNSUBSCRIBE, LIST, STATUS, and APPEND), the following commands are valid in the selected state: CLOSE, UNSELECT, EXPUNGE, SEARCH, FETCH, STORE, COPY, MOVE, and UID.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The CLOSE command permanently removes all messages that have the \Deleted flag set from the currently selected mailbox, and it returns to the authenticated state from the selected state.
actions: permanently remove messages with \Deleted flag from selected mailbox

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: No messages are removed, and no error is given, if the mailbox is selected by an EXAMINE command or is otherwise selected as read-only. The CLOSE command still returns to the authenticated state.
actions: return to authenticated state without expunge

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The SELECT command MAY be issued without previously issuing a CLOSE command. The SELECT command implicitly closes the currently selected mailbox without doing an expunge.
actions: implicitly close currently selected mailbox without expunge

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The EXAMINE command MAY be issued without previously issuing a CLOSE command. The EXAMINE command implicitly closes the currently selected mailbox without doing an expunge.
actions: implicitly close currently selected mailbox without expunge

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The LOGOUT command MAY be issued without previously issuing a CLOSE command. The LOGOUT command implicitly closes the currently selected mailbox without doing an expunge.
actions: implicitly close currently selected mailbox without expunge

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The UNSELECT command frees a session's resources associated with the selected mailbox and returns the server to the authenticated state. Result: OK - unselect completed, now in authenticated state.
actions: free session resources associated with selected mailbox

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Result: BAD - no mailbox selected, or argument supplied but none permitted.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: BAD - no mailbox selected, or argument supplied but none permitted. UNSELECT requires an active selected mailbox (no arguments accepted).

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The EXPUNGE command permanently removes all messages that have the \Deleted flag set from the currently selected mailbox. Before returning an OK to the client, an untagged EXPUNGE response is sent for each message that is removed.
actions: send untagged EXPUNGE response for each removed message

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Result: NO - expunge failure: can't expunge (e.g., permission denied)

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Result: BAD - command unknown or arguments invalid

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Result: OK - search completed; OPTIONAL untagged response: ESEARCH

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Any options not defined by extensions that the server supports MUST be rejected with a BAD response.
statements.trigger: SEARCH command with unsupported result option

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the server does not support the specified [CHARSET], it MUST return a tagged NO response (not a BAD). This response SHOULD contain the BADCHARSET response code, which MAY list the CHARSETs supported by the server.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: SAVE - This option tells the server to remember the result of the SEARCH or UID SEARCH command and store it in an internal variable that we will reference as the 'search result variable'.
statements.trigger: SEARCH command with SAVE result option
actions: store search results in search result variable

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The client can use the '$' marker to reference the content of this internal variable. The '$' marker can be used instead of message sequence or UID sequence in order to indicate that the server should substitute it with the list of messages from the search result variable.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the SEARCH results in no matches, the server MUST NOT include the MIN result option in the ESEARCH response; however, it still MUST send the ESEARCH response. (Applies equally to MAX and ALL result options.)
actions: omit MIN/MAX/ALL result options from ESEARCH

statements.subject: server
statements.description: In absence of any other SEARCH result option, the SAVE result option also suppresses any ESEARCH response that would have been otherwise returned by the SEARCH command.
statements.trigger: SEARCH command with SAVE as sole result option
actions: store results in search result variable

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Upon successful completion of a SELECT or an EXAMINE command (after the tagged OK response), the current search result variable is reset to the empty sequence.
actions: reset search result variable to empty sequence

statements.subject: session
statements.description: A successful SEARCH command with the SAVE result option sets the value of the search result variable to the list of messages found in the SEARCH command.
actions: set search result variable to list of messages found by SEARCH

statements.subject: session
statements.description: A SEARCH command that caused the server to return the BAD tagged response MUST NOT change the search result variable.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: A SEARCH command with no SAVE result option that caused the server to return NO tagged response MUST NOT change the search result variable.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: A successful SEARCH command with no SAVE result option MUST NOT change the search result variable.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: A SEARCH command with the SAVE result option that caused the server to return the NO tagged response sets the value of the search result variable to the empty sequence.
actions: set search result variable to empty sequence

statements.subject: session
statements.description: When a message listed in the search result variable is EXPUNGEd, it is automatically removed from the list.
actions: remove expunged message from search result variable

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If the server decides to send a new UIDVALIDITY value while the mailbox is opened, it causes the resetting of the search variable to the empty sequence.
actions: reset search result variable to empty sequence

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Use of a SEARCH RETURN (SAVE) command followed by a command using the "$" marker creates direct dependency between the two commands. A server MUST execute the two commands in the order they were received.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: A client MAY pipeline a SEARCH RETURN (SAVE) command with one or more commands using the "$" marker, as long as this doesn't create an ambiguity.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: In some cases, the server MAY refuse to save a SEARCH (SAVE) result, for example, if an internal limit on the number of saved results is reached. In this case, the server MUST return a tagged NO response containing the NOTSAVED response code and set the search result variable to the empty sequence.
actions: send tagged NO response with NOTSAVED response code
set search result variable to empty sequence

statements.subject: session
statements.description: the server MUST set the search result variable to the empty sequence when refusing to save a SEARCH (SAVE) result
statements.guard_semantics: server refuses to save SEARCH (SAVE) result

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Result: OK - fetch completed

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Result: NO - fetch error: can't fetch that data

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Result: BAD - command unknown or arguments invalid

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The \Seen flag is implicitly set; if this causes the flags to change, they SHOULD be included as part of the FETCH responses.
actions: include flags in FETCH response if changed

statements.subject: message
statements.description: BODY.PEEK[<section>]<<partial>> - An alternate form of BODY[<section>] that does not implicitly set the \Seen flag.
actions: send section body data without setting \Seen flag

statements.subject: message
statements.description: BINARY.PEEK[<section-binary>]<<partial>> - An alternate form of BINARY[<section-binary>] that does not implicitly set the \Seen flag.
actions: send decoded section binary data without setting \Seen flag

statements.subject: server
statements.description: COPY command copies the specified message(s) to the end of the specified destination mailbox; result OK - copy completed.
statements.trigger: COPY command with valid sequence set and existing destination mailbox

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the destination mailbox does not exist, a server MUST return an error. It MUST NOT automatically create the mailbox. Unless it is certain that the destination mailbox can not be created, the server MUST send the response code '[TRYCREATE]' as the prefix of the text of the tagged NO response.
statements.trigger: COPY command with non-existent destination mailbox
actions: send tagged NO response with [TRYCREATE] prefix

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the COPY command is unsuccessful for any reason, server implementations MUST restore the destination mailbox to its state before the COPY attempt, i.e., partial copy MUST NOT be done.
actions: restore destination mailbox to pre-COPY state

statements.subject: server
statements.description: On successful completion of a COPY, the server returns a COPYUID response code. In the case of a mailbox that has permissions set so that the client can COPY to the mailbox, but not SELECT or EXAMINE it, the server MUST NOT send a COPYUID response code as it would disclose information about the mailbox.
statements.guard_semantics: MUST be sent on COPY success unless mailbox.permission.select = false; MUST NOT be sent if client lacks SELECT or EXAMINE permission on destination; MAY be omitted if mailbox.status = UIDNOTSTICKY

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Result BAD - command unknown or arguments invalid.
statements.trigger: COPY command with unknown command or invalid arguments

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Result: OK - move completed; NO - move error: can't move those messages or to that name; BAD - command unknown or arguments invalid.
actions: server returns tagged OK, NO, or BAD

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the destination mailbox does not exist, a server MUST return an error. It MUST NOT automatically create the mailbox. Unless it is certain that the destination mailbox cannot be created, the server MUST send the response code "[TRYCREATE]" as the prefix of the text of the tagged NO response.
statements.trigger: MOVE command with nonexistent destination mailbox
actions: server sends tagged NO with [TRYCREATE] response code

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Servers are also REQUIRED to send the COPYUID response code in an untagged OK before sending EXPUNGE or similar responses.
actions: server sends untagged OK with COPYUID response code

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The server MUST leave each message in a state where it is in at least one of the source or target mailboxes (no message can be lost or orphaned). The server SHOULD NOT leave any message in both mailboxes.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The server may send EXPUNGE responses before the tagged response, so the client cannot safely send more commands with message sequence number arguments while the server is processing MOVE.
actions: client must not send commands with message sequence number arguments

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Though the COPY and EXPUNGE response codes will be returned, response codes for a STORE MUST NOT be generated, and the \Deleted flag MUST NOT be set for any message.
actions: server MUST NOT generate STORE response codes

statements.subject: session
statements.description: UID command with COPY, MOVE, FETCH, or STORE arguments using unique identifiers instead of message sequence numbers; a non-existent unique identifier is ignored without error. Result: OK - UID command completed; NO - UID command error; BAD - command unknown or arguments invalid.
statements.trigger: UID COPY | UID MOVE | UID FETCH | UID STORE
actions: process command using UIDs instead of sequence numbers

statements.subject: session
statements.description: UID EXPUNGE command permanently removes all messages that have both the \Deleted flag set and a UID included in the specified sequence set from the currently selected mailbox.
statements.post_cond: message.flag = \Deleted & message.uid IN sequence_set => message.permanently_removed = true

statements.subject: session
statements.description: UID SEARCH command returns unique identifiers instead of message sequence numbers in the ESEARCH response; the corresponding ESEARCH response MUST include the UID indicator.
actions: send untagged ESEARCH response with UID indicator and UIDs

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Server implementations MUST implicitly include the UID message data item as part of any FETCH response caused by a UID command, regardless of whether a UID was specified as a message data item to the FETCH.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: An example of unilateral untagged server data occurs when the IMAP connection is in the selected state.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: In the selected state, the server checks the mailbox for new messages as part of command execution. If new messages are found, the server sends an untagged EXISTS response reflecting the new size of the mailbox.
actions: send untagged EXISTS response with new mailbox size

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Server implementations that offer multiple simultaneous access to the same mailbox SHOULD also send appropriate unilateral untagged FETCH and EXPUNGE responses if another agent changes the state of any message flags or expunges any messages.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Command continuation request responses use the token '+' instead of a tag. These responses are sent by the server to indicate acceptance of an incomplete client command and readiness for the remainder of the command.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Tagged status responses indicate the completion result (OK, NO, or BAD status) of a client command and have a tag matching the command.
statements.post_cond: session.command_result = OK | session.command_result = NO | session.command_result = BAD
actions: send tagged status response (OK|NO|BAD) with matching command tag

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A server returns the CLOSED response code when the currently selected mailbox is closed implicitly using the SELECT or EXAMINE command on another mailbox. The CLOSED response code serves as a boundary between responses for the previously opened mailbox (which was closed) and the newly selected mailbox; all responses before the CLOSED response code relate to the mailbox that was closed, and all subsequent responses relate to the newly opened mailbox.
statements.trigger: SELECT or EXAMINE on another mailbox

statements.subject: session
statements.description: There is no need to return the CLOSED response code on completion of the CLOSE or the UNSELECT command (or similar), whose purpose is to close the currently selected mailbox without opening a new one.
actions: close currently selected mailbox without opening a new one

statements.subject: session
statements.description: READ-ONLY: The mailbox is selected as read-only, or its access while selected has changed from read-write to read-only.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: READ-WRITE: The mailbox is selected as read-write, or its access while selected has changed from read-only to read-write.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: PREAUTH and BYE are always untagged.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: PREAUTH and BYE are always untagged.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The untagged form is also used as one of three possible greetings at connection startup. It indicates that the connection is not yet authenticated and that a LOGIN or an AUTHENTICATE command is needed.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The untagged OK form is used as one of three possible greetings at connection startup. It indicates that the connection is not yet authenticated and that a LOGIN or an AUTHENTICATE command is needed.
statements.trigger: untagged OK greeting at connection startup

statements.subject: session
statements.description: When tagged, the OK response indicates successful completion of the associated command.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: When tagged, the NO response indicates unsuccessful completion of the associated command.
actions: send tagged NO with human-readable text

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The untagged form of NO indicates a warning; the command can still complete successfully.
actions: send untagged NO with human-readable warning text

statements.subject: message
statements.description: NO response contents: OPTIONAL response code, human-readable text.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The PREAUTH response is always untagged and is one of three possible greetings at connection startup. It indicates that the connection has already been authenticated by external means; thus, no LOGIN/AUTHENTICATE command is needed. Because PREAUTH moves the connection directly to the authenticated state.
statements.trigger: PREAUTH greeting received at connection startup
actions: connection transitions to Authenticated state without LOGIN or AUTHENTICATE

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Clients that require mandatory TLS MUST close the connection after receiving the PREAUTH response on a non-protected port.
statements.trigger: PREAUTH received on non-protected port with mandatory TLS required
statements.pre_cond: connection.state = Authenticated & connection.tls_protected = false & client.mandatory_tls = true

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Because PREAUTH moves the connection directly to the authenticated state, it effectively prevents the client from using the STARTTLS command.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: As part of a normal logout sequence, the server will close the connection after sending the tagged OK response to the LOGOUT command.
statements.trigger: BYE sent during normal logout sequence
actions: send tagged OK response to LOGOUT

statements.subject: server
statements.description: As a panic shutdown announcement, the server closes the connection immediately after sending BYE.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: As an announcement of an inactivity autologout, the server closes the connection immediately after sending BYE.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: As one of three possible greetings at connection startup, indicating that the server is not willing to accept a connection from this client, the server closes the connection immediately.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The BYE response is always untagged and indicates that the server is about to close the connection.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: In all cases, the client SHOULD continue to read response data from the server until the connection is closed; this will ensure that any pending untagged or completion responses are read and processed.
actions: continue reading response data until connection is closed

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server will respond with a tagged NO response to any attempt to use the LOGIN command even if the user name and password are valid when LOGINDISABLED is advertised.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: An IMAP client MUST NOT issue the LOGIN command if the server advertises the LOGINDISABLED capability.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The LOGINDISABLED capability indicates that the LOGIN command is disabled.
statements.guard_semantics: When present, prohibits client from issuing LOGIN command

statements.subject: server
statements.description: It is quite common for the server to change the list of capabilities after successful TLS negotiation (STARTTLS command).

statements.subject: server
statements.description: It is quite common for the server to change the list of capabilities after successful authentication (AUTHENTICATE or LOGIN commands).
actions: send updated CAPABILITY response code in tagged OK

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A server MAY send capabilities automatically, by using the CAPABILITY response code in the initial PREAUTH or OK responses.
actions: include CAPABILITY response code in greeting

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A server MAY send capabilities automatically by sending an updated CAPABILITY response code in the tagged OK response as part of a successful authentication.
actions: include updated CAPABILITY response code in tagged OK response

statements.subject: client
statements.description: It is unnecessary for a client to send a separate CAPABILITY command if it recognizes these automatic capabilities and there was no change to the TLS and/or authentication state since they were received.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: An EXPUNGE response MUST NOT be sent when no command is in progress

statements.subject: server
statements.description: An EXPUNGE response MUST NOT be sent while responding to a FETCH, STORE, or SEARCH command
statements.pre_cond: server.active_command = FETCH | server.active_command = STORE | server.active_command = SEARCH

statements.subject: server
statements.description: An EXPUNGE response MAY be sent during a UID command (UID FETCH, UID STORE, UID SEARCH are different commands from FETCH, STORE, SEARCH)
statements.pre_cond: server.active_command = UID_FETCH | server.active_command = UID_STORE | server.active_command = UID_SEARCH

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A command is not 'in progress' until the complete command has been received; in particular, a command is not 'in progress' during the negotiation of command continuation
statements.guard_semantics: server.command_in_progress = true only after complete command received and not during continuation negotiation

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The update from the EXPUNGE response MUST be remembered by the client
actions: decrement message sequence numbers for all successive messages

statements.subject: server
statements.description: This form of response indicates that the server is ready to accept the continuation of a command from the client. This response is used in the AUTHENTICATE command to transmit server data to the client and request additional client data. This response is also used if an argument to any command is a synchronizing literal.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client is not permitted to send the octets of the synchronizing literal unless the server indicates that it is expected.
actions: client sends remainder of command including CRLF

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The command continuation request response is indicated by a '+' token instead of a tag.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Server sends greeting '* OK [CAPABILITY STARTTLS AUTH=SCRAM-SHA-256 LOGINDISABLED IMAP4rev2] IMAP4rev2 Service Ready' upon connection establishment on a non-TLS port.
actions: send greeting with CAPABILITY including STARTTLS, AUTH=SCRAM-SHA-256, LOGINDISABLED, IMAP4rev2

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Client issues STARTTLS; server responds OK 'Proceed with TLS negotiation'; TLS negotiation follows.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Client issues AUTHENTICATE SCRAM-SHA-256; after SASL exchange, server responds 'A001 OK SCRAM-SHA-256 authentication successful'.
actions: send tagged OK SCRAM-SHA-256 authentication successful

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Client issues SELECT inbox; server responds '* LIST', '* EXISTS', '* FLAGS', '* OK [UIDVALIDITY ...]', and tagged 'a002 OK [READ-WRITE] SELECT completed'.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Client issues LOGOUT; server responds '* BYE IMAP4rev2 server terminating connection' followed by 'a006 OK LOGOUT completed'.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: command-nonauth = login / authenticate / "STARTTLS" ; Valid only when in Not Authenticated state

statements.subject: session
statements.description: command-auth = append / create / delete / enable / examine / list / namespace-command / rename / select / status / subscribe / unsubscribe / idle ; Valid only in Authenticated or Selected state

statements.subject: session
statements.description: command-select = "CLOSE" / "UNSELECT" / "EXPUNGE" / copy / move / fetch / store / search / uid ; Valid only when in Selected state

statements.subject: session
statements.description: command = tag SP (command-any / command-auth / command-nonauth / command-select) CRLF ; Modal based on state

statements.subject: session
statements.description: command-any = "CAPABILITY" / "LOGOUT" / "NOOP" ; Valid in all states

statements.subject: session
statements.description: command-nonauth = login / authenticate / "STARTTLS" ; Valid only when in Not Authenticated state

statements.subject: session
statements.description: command-auth = append / create / delete / enable / examine / list / namespace-command / rename / select / status / subscribe / unsubscribe / idle ; Valid only in Authenticated or Selected state

statements.subject: session
statements.description: command-select = "CLOSE" / "UNSELECT" / "EXPUNGE" / copy / move / fetch / store / search / uid ; Valid only when in Selected state

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: response-fatal = "*" SP resp-cond-bye CRLF ; Server closes connection immediately

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Both the client and server MUST check the result of the STARTTLS command and subsequent TLS negotiation to see whether acceptable authentication and/or privacy was achieved.
statements.trigger: STARTTLS command result and TLS negotiation completion
actions: check TLS negotiation outcome for acceptable authentication and/or privacy

statements.subject: client
statements.description: During the TLS negotiation, the client MUST check its understanding of the server hostname against the server's identity as presented in the server Certificate message, in order to prevent on-path attackers attempting to masquerade as the server.
actions: verify server hostname against server Certificate message identity

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the server listens on a cleartext port, it MUST allow the STARTTLS command on it.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The server MUST implement TLS negotiation on an Implicit TLS port.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: IMAP4rev2 clients SHOULD try both ports 993 and 143 (and both IPv4 and IPv6) concurrently by default, unless overridden by either user configuration or DNS SRV records.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Many server responses and response codes are only meaningful in authenticated or even selected state.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Many server responses and response codes are only meaningful in authenticated or even selected state.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Before authentication, clients SHOULD ignore any responses other than CAPABILITY and server status responses (Section 7.1), as well as any response codes other than CAPABILITY.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Clients SHOULD ignore the ALERT response code until after TLS (whether using STARTTLS or TLS negotiation on an Implicit TLS port) or a SASL security layer with confidentiality protection has been successfully negotiated.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Unless explicitly allowed by an IMAP extension, when not in selected state, clients MUST ignore responses / response codes related to message and mailbox status such as FLAGS, EXIST, EXPUNGE, and FETCH.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Nothing prevents a server (or an on-path attacker) from sending such invalid responses in cleartext before STARTTLS/AUTHENTICATE commands are issued. Before authentication, clients SHOULD ignore any responses other than CAPABILITY and server status responses.
actions: expand set of processable server responses
